purpose: Define how any LLM or Human turns the Skin V1 token, composition, anatomy and surface declaration layers into a comparable UI specification sheet.
interpretationRules: Do not invent a navigation region because a column or list exists.
Do not invent extra menus, toolbars, tabs, fields, cards or panels not permitted by the surface declaration.
Illustrative content may fill a declared content region only when the declaration marks exampleContentPolicy=illustrative.
Literal labels and region names must be copied exactly when marked literal.
Use token names and measurements from the authorities; do not substitute a local palette, radius, font or border system.
Show the semantic role of each region in annotations: navigation, content, inspector, timeline, control, context, evidence or reference.
Show title/eyebrow/subtitle placement exactly as declared.
Show return placement exactly as declared.
A spec sheet is explanatory evidence, not a new visual authority.
Rendered geometry is evidence against this four-layer specification stack; it never becomes a fifth design authority.
Menu orientation, keyboard cues, frame thickness, gutters, columns and typography roles must resolve from existing profiles/declarations before a rendered comparison is made.

contentPolicies.controlledVocabulary: May choose only from declaration-provided values.
contentPolicies.illustrative: May invent neutral example content that does not change structure, navigation or semantics.

validationQuestions: Can a reviewer identify which regions are destination navigation versus content selection?
Can a reviewer identify the single primary work region?
Are title, subtitle, eyebrow and context metadata in their declared zones?
Does the board preserve declared column counting rather than visual guesswork?
Do nested regions remain subordinate instead of becoming new surfaces?
Would another LLM receiving the same inputs produce the same region map even if example text differs?
Can a reviewer compare expected versus rendered frame, gutter, column, menu and typography measurements without inspecting CSS manually?
Are structural overlap and scroll/panel findings expressed as evidence rather than inferred navigation semantics?
